newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary beet crop seen down to 3.8 mln t-industry.
newsitem.headline: Hungary beet crop seen down to 3.8 mln t-industry.

text.p: Hungary's sugar beet crop is expected to drop to some 3.8 million tonnes from last year's 4.6 million tonnes, Andras Angeli, Chairman of the Sugar Industry Association (SIA) said on Wednesday.
"Supposing an average sugar content, that would translate into 456,000 tonnes of sugar," Angeli told Reuters.
Last year Hungary's sugar output was 564,344 tonnes, he said, adding that domestic sugar demand was between 420,000 and 450,000 tonnes.
Angeli said the planted area was down to 96,471 hectares from last year's 110,742 hectares.
He said that despite a slow start, beet growth was satisfactory at the moment.

"Due to the rainy summer, sugar beet has recouped the two-week delay delay caused by a very cold spring," Angeli said. "If the beet receives another 40 to 50 millimetres of rain this month, normal growth will be assured".

He said that although the SIA received a small batch of results from the first beet test recently, it did not release them as the results were not indicative enough due to the small number of samples.
"We only received test results from about one third of the planted area and that would not make for an appropriate estimate," Angeli said.
He added that the second beet test, that would produce the first conclusive result was expected around August 15.
